kanban-claude 0.4.0.dev2

A small release that comes from looking at how the roles really ran after 0.4.0.dev1. A followed log in kanban web no longer ends short of its last lines. A warden that reviews a PR on its own can now ask for changes. And a designer on a repo where the browser server is switched off is reported by kanban doctor and has a fallback.

Release explainer, 2026-10-21. Diff v0.4.0.dev1 (c113116) to 90163da, the tip of main. This is a pre-release. The version bump to 0.4.0.dev2, the changelog heading and the releases row come after the diff and are not part of it.

  • 3

    fixes, one each for the web log view, the warden and the designer

  • 5

    commits from two merged PRs, #9 and #10, changing 13 files

  • +114
    −22

    lines added and removed, the changelog and README included

  • 22

    doctor checks, up from 21: check 22 is new

  • +3

    test functions (two in test_store.py, one in test_doctor.py); no schema change, no new config key, no new verb

Background

Where these three fixes came from

The owner runs the board every day, and every dispatched run is a paid claude -p session. After 0.4.0.dev1 an Opus review went through the roles and checked what it found against the run history of the live board. It found two problems with roles. The owner found a third while watching a run in kanban web. Each one cost time or turns on real cards, and none needs a schema change.

  • Web. When a followed run finished on a narrow screen, the transcript stopped scrolling and ended up to 42 px short of its last lines.
  • Warden. A warden can be dispatched on a card of its own, to review a PR that no card of the board builds. There is no builder to send the PR back to, so kanban request-changes was refused. Five live warden runs worked around it by writing a needs_input block by hand.
  • Designer. The designer brings its own browser server, but on a repo where the owner had turned playwright off, a designer run started with no browser at all.

The walkthrough takes them in that order. Line numbers are in the files at 90163da unless a path says otherwise.

Change diagram

Which components changed, and how

  • + added
  • ~ changed
  • ! fixed
  • = left as it was

Top two rows, the designer. The runner launches the designer session with its own mcp/designer.json. The dashed arrow is Claude Code, not this plugin: the account's .claude.json lists servers to turn off for a repo, and that list also reaches the card worktrees inside it, so it cuts in on the session. Check 22 of kanban doctor reads the server names the designer brings and that list, and finds the file through the runner's account_json(). Third row, the warden. kanban request-changes now looks at the run first: the reviewer role's work run, a card with no builder, ends in a block; a review run goes to the builder as before. Bottom row, the web log view and the files that follow the other changes. On a narrow screen the boxes stack in one column in the same order, without arrows.

Walkthrough

Three problems, one at a time

Each area says what changed, why, and how you notice it as the operator.

A followed log stays on its last line when the box resizes !fixed

What changed
In the constructor of Transcript (webui/logview.js:59) the log box, this.el, gets a ResizeObserver whose callback is this.toBottom(). destroy() disconnects it (:121). The call passes no force, so toBottom() (:114) scrolls only while follow is on. The scroll listener above it is untouched: scrolling more than 120 px from the end switches follow off, and from then on a resize leaves the view where it is. The observer watches the size of the box, not its content, so new lines still reach the bottom through tick() as before. The dock under the board uses the same class with follow: true (dock.js:52), so it gets the fix as well. The raw log (RawLog) is not changed.
Why
Two things lined up. When a run ends, update() in logsPanel rebuilds the run picker's option text from runLabel(), which turns (running) into (completed). The Follow button is hidden only when the panel is mounted, not on update, so it is still in the toolbar. On a narrow screen the longer label wrapped the toolbar onto a second row. The log box takes the space that is left (.logs-body .tx { flex: 1 }), so it got shorter, but the old code only scrolled when a line arrived or the button was pressed, and a finished run sends no more lines. The bottom edge of the box moved up by the height of the new row and hid the end of the transcript. A window resize or a rotated phone does the same.
How you notice it
Open the Logs tab of a running card in a narrow window with Follow on and wait for the run to end: the last lines stay in view. Narrow the window while following: the same. Scroll up first, then narrow it: the view stays where you left it. The diff adds no test for this; it is a change in browser behaviour that the Python suite does not exercise, so check it by eye.

A warden on a card with no builder can ask for changes ~changed+added=frozen

What changed
request_changes() in store.py:2149 now begins, inside its transaction, by reading the run's kind and role. If it is a work run and the role is the configured reviewer (dispatch.reviewer, warden by default), it returns block(conn, run_id, "needs_input", f"CHANGES REQUESTED: {reason}") and stops. tx() (:394) joins a transaction that is already open, so the block runs inside the verb's own. The card ends blocked with block_kind needs_input, its assignee stays the warden, and the comment reads BLOCKED: CHANGES REQUESTED: <reason>, since block() adds the first prefix. Everything else is as it was. A review run still goes to the builder as ready or todo. A work run of a builder, smith or designer, still reaches the old refusal, request-changes is for review runs. A second call is a no-op: the run has ended with terminal verb block, so _verb_run returns nothing and the verb returns {"noop": True}. Because it is block(), the loop guard (BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT, 2) applies as it does to a hand-written block, and the event is the ordinary blocked one, so the GitHub and Jira sync sees a normal block. Four text files follow: agents/warden.md and skills/kanban-code-review/SKILL.md get one sentence after the request-changes line, skills/kanban/references/cli.md changes the verb's row, and skills/kanban/SKILL.md gets a row for the orchestrator: a blocked card with CHANGES REQUESTED: on a warden card with no builder means the reasons go to the PR's author, and after they push, kanban unblock <id> --reason "<what changed>" runs the warden again.
Why
The warden's own instructions end with request-changes when it has findings. On a card of its own there is no implementer to send the card back to, so the verb refused, and the warden had to improvise. Five live runs wrote the needs_input block by hand. Now the verb does it, with a fixed prefix that the orchestrator's skill can match, and the warden's instructions stay the same.
How you notice it
A warden card in Needs you whose comment starts BLOCKED: CHANGES REQUESTED:. test_warden_work_run_request_changes_blocks_for_the_owner (test_store.py:217) checks the status, block kind, assignee, the exact comment and the no-op on a repeat. test_builder_work_run_request_changes_is_refused (:228) checks that a builder still gets the refusal.

A designer without a browser: a better prompt, a doctor check ~changed+added=frozen

What changed
Three parts, plus one thing deliberately left alone.

The prompt. Step 6 of agents/designer.md now says to verify in Chromium and in WebKit, and lists the checks: a narrow phone and a wide desktop width, focus order and visible focus, empty, loading and error states, console errors, prefers-reduced-motion, and every dialog. A dialog must open, close, cancel, and stay open on a click inside it. Screenshots are cropped, with browser_take_screenshot given an element or locator.screenshot() in a script. WebKit has no MCP tool here, so it always goes through a script. When the playwright MCP tools are missing, the designer does the same for everything: once per run uv run --no-project --with playwright python -m playwright install chromium webkit, then each script with uv run --no-project --with playwright python <script>, its screenshots under $TMPDIR and never in the repo.

The helper. runner.account_json(config_dir) (runner.py:175) returns the account's .claude.json: ~/.claude.json for the default ~/.claude, else <dir>/.claude.json. The code was inline in mcp_config() (:185), which now calls the helper. In doctor.py, claude_in(d) (:109) builds what the owner types to start Claude on an account, and check 9 uses it where it had an inline version of the same string; its output does not change.

Check 22 (doctor.py:528), designer's browser MCP. If the designer is not an active role it passes with designer is not dispatched. Otherwise it reads the server names from mcp/designer.json (playwright). Then, for every config directory that boards use and every repo of those boards, it reads projects[<repo>].disabledMcpServers in that account's .claude.json, matching the repo's top-level path as text. For each hit it warns, never fails, so the exit code stays 0. The detail and fix of a hit look like this, with an invented board and path:detail acme-web: /Users/you/src/acme-web turns off playwright, so designer checks pages with a Playwright script fix cd /Users/you/src/acme-web && claude, then /mcp and enable playwrightWith an account that is not the default, the fix starts with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=… claude. Doctor now has 22 checks, and the README says so.

Left alone. The runner still passes --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config with the designer's file (runner.py:329), and mcp/designer.json is unchanged. Renaming the designer's server so that the repo's off switch no longer matches it would have given a browser back, and was not done: the switch is the owner's choice, so the doctor tells him and he decides.
Why
The designer's browser server comes from the plugin, not from the repo, so one would expect the repo's settings not to reach it. They do. Claude Code applies the repo's projects[<repo>].disabledMcpServers from the account's .claude.json to the card worktrees inside the repo as well. On a repo where the owner had turned playwright off for his own sessions, the init event of a designer run showed playwright: disabled and the run had no browser. The designer has to verify what it builds, so it needs a way to do so either way, and the owner needs to be told, before a paid run, that the server is off.
How you notice it
Run kanban doctor. A repo that turns the server off gives a warning on line 22 with the fix; run it, and check 22 passes. test_a_board_repo_that_turns_off_the_designer_browser_warns_check_22 (test_doctor.py:570) writes a .claude.json that disables atlassian and playwright for the board's repo, expects the warning with code == 0 and that exact fix, then drops the designer from dispatch.roles and expects the pass. The healthy-install test now expects 22 passes.

Upgrade notes

Moving from 0.4.0.dev1 to 0.4.0.dev2

  1. Run /kanban-claude:setup between cards, as for dev1, so the daemon and the CLI move together. The diff changes no table and no config key: the schema stays at 7, so there is no migration and no backup.
  2. Run kanban doctor. If check 22 warns, run the fix it prints (cd <repo> && claude, then /mcp and enable playwright) if you want the designer to have its browser server there; otherwise leave it, and the designer falls back to a script.
  3. If kanban web is running, restart it and reload the page, so the browser loads the new logview.js.
  4. A warden card you blocked or unblocked by hand before this version is as you left it. Only a new request-changes call from a warden's work run changes.

Quiz

Check what you took from this page

Six questions. Pick an answer to see the explanation.

1. Why did a followed transcript end up short of its last lines when the run finished?

Only a new line or the Follow button called toBottom(), and a finished run sends no lines. The box lost a row of height and its bottom edge moved up over the end of the transcript.

2. You scroll up in a followed log, then narrow the window. Where is the view afterwards?

The scroll listener turns follow off once you are more than 120 px from the end, and toBottom(force) moves the view only when force or follow is set (logview.js:114).

3. A warden reviews a PR on a card of its own and calls kanban request-changes. What happens now?

The verb sees a work run of the reviewer role and hands over to block() in the same transaction (store.py:2149). With no builder, the owner is the one who can reach the PR's author.

4. A smith work run calls kanban request-changes. What happens?

The new branch is for the configured reviewer's work run only. A builder's work run reaches the old check, and test_builder_work_run_request_changes_is_refused keeps it that way.

5. A designer run's init event shows playwright: disabled, though the designer brings its own server. Why?

The runner's flags and designer.json were fine and are unchanged. The repo-level off switch reaches the worktrees, and kanban doctor check 22 now reports the repo and prints the fix.

6. Why does check 22 warn and print a fix instead of renaming the designer's server, which would give it a browser back?

That was deliberately not done. The designer meanwhile has the script fallback for Chromium and WebKit, and the owner decides whether to enable the server for the repo. A warning leaves the exit code at 0.
